QF.id: Cat III AIF Due Diligence and Risk_2

question.text: Evaluating a hedge fund manager's track record requires assessing:

answer.text: Sharpe, maximum drawdown, historical returns over at least five years, sizeable corpus/AUM, investment-team experience, disciplinary history, and key-person dependency

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook lays out a multi-factor framework for manager due diligence: risk-adjusted return measures such as Sharpe, drawdown tolerance via maximum drawdown, a historical track record (with sizeable corpus and returning investors over time), the experience of the investment team and key personnel, and a clean disciplinary record. Manager selection rests on triangulating these factors, not on any single number. The Trap: Looking only at gross returns ignores the risk taken to earn them; looking only at AUM tells you size but not skill; looking only at year-1 returns ignores consistency and drawdown behaviour over longer horizons. Note: Manager-evaluation factors (Sharpe, max drawdown, track record length, corpus, investment-team experience, disciplinary history, key-person risk) are drawn from the AIF (Category III) Distributors workbook.
